title: Kernel-sensing prefill arbiter and loopback fallback for speculative decoding
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Goal: implement a kernel-aware prefill arbiter that probes candidate model variants with a lightweight kernel-sensing probe, scores their expected acceptance probability and latency budget, and routes speculative decode traffic to the highest-value candidate while retaining a fast loopback fallback to a conservative model if acceptance criteria fail. This ticket covers design, prototype, telemetry, and a staged rollout.

Background: our current speculative decode experiments show large variance in accept rates across kernel builds and sequence-length distributions. We need a runtime-level arbiter that can detect kernel behavior (e.g., fp16 vs int8 kernel stalls, fused-attention fast-paths) at request time and make routing decisions without adding >2ms median overhead to prefill.

Scope: (1) implement a micro-prober that executes a tiny prefill on candidate model variants to extract kernel fingerprint signals (kernel type, first-token latency, kv-cache warmup delta); (2) scoring function that combines expected acceptance, tail-latency risk, and cost delta into a single routing score; (3) loopback fallback that can cancel speculative branch and commit to conservative decode with minimal token duplication; (4) instrumentation and SLI mapping; (5) simulation harness and canary rollout plan.

Non-goals: heavy-weight offline model selection, changes to model architecture, or global autoscaler changes. This ticket remains runtime-level.

Risks & trade-offs: lightweight probing risks perturbing latency SLOs; aggressive routing increases cost and potential quality regressions if acceptance scoring is noisy. We favor conservative thresholds for first canaries and provide an emergency circuit-breaker to disable probing per-customer or per-route.

Planned deliverables: design doc, prototype PR with micro-prober and scoring function, benchmark results, telemetry dashboards, rollout playbook, and a kill-switch API.
acceptance_criteria: Micro-prober adds <2ms median overhead to prefill path (measured at p95 <5ms)
Routing decisions increase overall token acceptance for canary workload by >=10% without >5% cost increase
Loopback fallback completes with <=1 token duplication on average and no request-level errors
Telemetry surface: per-candidate acceptance_rate, probe_latency, fallback_rate (all exported to console)
Canary rollout plan documented and automated via runtime feature flag
updates: 2026-03-01: Ticket created after architecture sync (notes in design doc). Assigned Miguel for prototype. Estimate 8pt.
2026-03-03: Spike: implemented micro-prober PoC that emits kernel fingerprint (kernel_name, aten_version, fused_attn_flag) using 32-token warmup. Prototype added to experimental runtime branch.
2026-03-06: Bench results vs baseline on rtx-a100: probe median 1.6ms, p95 4.7ms. Observed accept-signal correlation of 0.62 for our internal langchain-like prompt set.

2026-03-08: Design review with Runtime and ML teams. Decision: use weighted-logistic scorer combining acceptance_prob, delta_cost, and tail_latency_risk. We will expose per-route thresholds so PMs can tune conservatism.

2026-03-10: Implemented loopback prototype with token deduplication using ephemeral sequence-id. Early tests show average 0.7 duplicated tokens on fallback; edge cases around simultaneous fallback requests noted.
2026-03-12: Instrumentation added: new metrics (probe_latency_ms, probe_accept_score, speculative_routed, fallback_count). Dashboard draft available.

2026-03-14: Blocker: observed rare race where fallback cancellation triggers duplicate commit; writing a targeted unit test and patch. Plan canary on internal dev account after fix.

Review notes: PM (Lina Ortega) requested per-customer opt-out toggle and explicit cost accounting for speculative runs. Design doc link and PRs below.
notes: Implementation detail: probe uses a capped 8-token micro-prefill and samples only 10% of warm traffic by default. Sampling rate configurable per-route.
Fallback strategy: soft-fallback first attempts to merge speculative tokens if acceptance proven; otherwise roll back and resubmit to conservative model variant. This minimizes visible duplication.
Operational playbook: add runtime feature flag 'spec.probe.enable' and emergency 'spec.probe.kill' per-customer. Rollout will be 1% -> 5% -> 20% canary progression with health checks at each step.
